The Lloyd-Davies position with Trendelenburg can be a disaster waiting to happen due to the profound ischemia of the lower limbs that it causes. The modification of lithotomy positions during pelvic surgery is not associated with lower limb ischemia, but adding the Trendelenburg position significantly increases this risk. During recovery, hyperperfusion confined to muscle compartments may put patients at risk of developing lower limb compartment syndrome.

This can lead to significant morbidity and potentially long-term damage to the affected limbs if left untreated or inadequately managed. It is essential to carefully consider alternative positions during pelvic surgery to minimize this risk.

In summary, while modifications to lithotomy positions might be beneficial for certain procedures, the Lloyd-Davies position with Trendelenburg should be approached with caution and only considered when other alternatives are not feasible or possible.
